summary: A wallchart of who is away: one new read endpoint GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/time-off/calendar and one new screen at /org/{orgId}/time-off/calendar, rows are active memberships and columns are consecutive calendar days, with a band per approved (solid) or pending (hatched) VacationRequest and holiday/weekend shading. Behind it sits the change that costs the most: a member's holiday country stops being Account.phoneCountryCode and becomes Membership.countryCode falling back to Organization.countryCode — two new nullable columns, one shared helper, and four already-shipping call sites that must all adopt it, two of which move what Amounts Owed pays. Both countries get a picker: the organization's on Settings > Holidays behind a new GET/PUT pair, the member's on their About tab riding the member update that already ships. One new capability in both capability unions, one sidebar row, one additive migration. The calendar writes nothing. REPLAN, round 2: the country-write rule the review halted on is settled in the document - both writes test the uppercase shape AND membership of the assigned ISO 3166-1 list, so an unassigned code such as XX is refused, and both refusals carry PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid rather than HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.countryCodeInvalid, whose text is false of XX. Two code blockers are planned with it: the calendar screen resolves today from the caller's Account.timezone rather than the browser clock, and a failed read is reported as a failed read rather than as an empty scope.

tasks.title: Schema and the one migration — two nullable country columns
tasks.detail: Membership.countryCode String? @db.Char(2) and Organization.countryCode String? @db.Char(2) — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, uppercase, nullable with NO default and NO backfill (contracts, Data Model). Doc-comment each the way the neighbouring columns are: Membership's is the first link of the holiday-country chain (REQ-01-026), null meaning 'use the organization's'; Organization's is the second. No new table, no index, no altered column. Write the migration SQL by hand in the style of apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260901130000_spec_org_03_holidays/migration.sql — two ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN "countryCode" CHAR(2) statements and a header saying why it is additive. This run writes exactly one migration; do not add a second in any later task.

migration.note: infra/deploy.sh runs infra/migrate.sh as a one-off ECS task on the NEW image (deploy.sh:175-185, guarded on `api` being among the services deployed) and only then `tf apply`s the services (:187-192) — the schema changes while the PREVIOUS code is still serving, which is why the header at deploy.sh:27 states migrations run BEFORE the rollout. Both columns are nullable with no default and nothing backfills them, so old code against the new schema simply never selects them and a code rollback needs no database rollback. The migration step is skipped entirely on a web-only deploy.

concurrency.lock: none — DDL only; the row locks are named on T4 and T5

tasks.title: packages/validation — the messages, the capability in both unions, the country chain, the range and preset arithmetic
tasks.detail: Four pieces, all in packages/validation because both surfaces re-run them and because npm run test:unit runs this workspace and nothing else. (1) NEW MODULE packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts, beside holiday-messages.ts and re-exported from index.ts: TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES with exactly the eleven rows of the Error Messages table (rangeRequired, rangeInverted, rangeTooWide, scopeInvalid, teamsRequired, peopleRequired, tooManyMembers, emptyStateTitle, emptyStateBody, orgCountryHint, memberCountryDefaultOption), verbatim; TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MAX_RANGE_DAYS = 92 and TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MAX_MEMBERS = 100; the scope union 'all'|'teams'|'people' with its validator (REQ-01-041); a range validator answering Validation Rules 1-4 IN THE TABLE'S ORDER and returning the FIRST failure only (contracts: 'a request that is both inverted and scoped everyone is refused with rangeInverted and nothing else') — it compares raw ISO dates and returns no timezone-shifted instant, which is REQ-01-017's half of the contract and the opposite of validateReportRange; the three window presets (Week, 2 weeks, Month) computed from a firstDayOfWeek of 'Monday'|'Sunday' plus the back/forward/today steps of REQ-01-049, where Week and 2 weeks move one preset length and Month moves a whole calendar month; and a band accessible-name builder in the mock's order ('Vacation · approved · 2026-09-14 – 2026-09-18 · 5 working days'), so no screen writes that string inline. (2) roles.ts: add 'ViewTimeOffCalendar' to the Capability union and to ROLE_CAPABILITIES for admin, manager and user — not viewer. (3) index.ts: add 'view-time-off-calendar' to MemberCapability and write it into all four rows of CAPABILITY_MATRIX (true, true, true, false). Both unions are exhaustive against their tables, so the compiler names every row you miss. (4) reports.ts: export resolveMemberHolidayCountry(membershipCountry, organizationCountry) — both arguments REQUIRED, neither defaulted. It answers REQ-01-026/027/040: return the membership's value when it normalizes to a real ISO alpha-2, else the organization's when it does, else null; the result is always UPPERCASE ('pl' -> 'PL'), and a value that is two letters but not an assigned code ('XX') does NOT normalize. Use validateCountryCode from autofill.ts (packages/validation/src/autofill.ts:683 — it upcases and tests membership of COUNTRY_NAMES, the 249-code list) as the normalizer; do NOT use validateHolidayCountryCode here, which is the WRITE rule and accepts any two uppercase letters. isHolidayApplicableToMember already ships at reports.ts:509 and is unchanged. (5) REPLAN, round 2 - VALIDATION RULE 9, which the contracts settle as TWO tests and not one, exported once and called by both writes: validateStatedCountryCode(input) in packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts. null, undefined and a blank string are valid and normalize to null (REQ-01-034, REQ-01-043); a non-string is invalid; then the UPPERCASE SHAPE, /^[A-Z]{2}$/ against the raw value, so 'pl' is REFUSED rather than upcased (Edge case 11 rests on this); then MEMBERSHIP OF THE ASSIGNED ISO 3166-1 LIST through validateCountryCode (packages/validation/src/autofill.ts:683), so 'XX' is refused though its shape is right (REQ-01-036, REQ-01-051, Edge case 10). Every failure carries PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid ('Enter a valid country', autofill.ts:510) and never HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.countryCodeInvalid, whose text ('must be 2 uppercase letters') is false of the value it would be refusing. COMPOSE validateCountryCode; do not copy COUNTRY_NAMES - one country list, one definition. Do NOT change validateHolidayCountryCode: a holiday ROW's country keeps it (holidays.service.ts:322, HolidayModal.tsx:222), because there the code is a label matched against a resolved country and an unassigned one reaches nobody, which is visible and harmless. These two columns are the INPUT to that resolution, which is why they are the strict ones.

tasks.title: GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/time-off/calendar — the read the whole screen is
tasks.detail: Controller: @Controller('api/organizations/:orgId') with @UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard) and one @Get('time-off/calendar') — copy HolidaysController's stack exactly. NO RequireCapability and NO CapabilityGuard: the refusal must be a bare 404 (REQ-01-002) byte-identical to the wrong-organization one (REQ-01-039), and CapabilityGuard answers 403. Gate in the service, in the shape of HolidaysService.requireViewCapability (holidays.service.ts:239): load the caller's membership by session.accountId, refuse a non-active or wrong-organization row, then `if (!can(normalizeRole(caller.role), 'view-time-off-calendar')) throw new NotFoundException()`. NORMALIZE — a membership still storing 'member' must be answered 200 (TC-01-UNIT-04). Every query filters by session.organizationId; the path :orgId is never a selector. Validation runs in the Validation Rules table's order and the FIRST failure is the whole answer, thrown as 422 `{ error: 'validation_error', fields: { <field>: <message> } }` (the shape ReportsService.parseQuery emits at reports.service.ts:615): startDate/endDate -> rangeRequired, range -> rangeInverted then rangeTooWide, scope -> scopeInvalid, projectIds -> teamsRequired, memberIds -> peopleRequired, scope -> tooManyMembers (rule 8, checked last, after the rows resolve). Row resolution: scope=all is every active membership of the caller's organization; scope=teams is every active membership with a ProjectMember row on one of the named projects, PLUS — when projectIds contains the literal sentinel 'none' — every active membership with no ProjectMember row on any NON-ARCHIVED project (REQ-01-007; the named-project branch never consults the archived flag, Edge case 5), duplicates collapsed to one row (Edge case 6); scope=people is the named memberships. Foreign ids are intersected away silently (REQ-01-010) and 'removed' memberships never appear (REQ-01-011). Order by display name case-insensitively (REQ-01-012). Days: compare VacationRequest.startDate/endDate and Holiday.date against UTC-midnight @db.Date bounds built from the raw ISO strings, `new Date(`${iso}T00:00:00.000Z`)`, the way HolidaysService.listHolidays does — never validateReportRange's timezone-shifted startUtc, which is exactly the boundary drop TC-01-INT-10 is built to catch. range.today comes from the caller's Account.timezone via Intl, falling back to UTC when it is null, empty or unrecognized (REQ-01-018, the currentYearIn idiom at holidays.service.ts:358). days[] carries date, isWeekend (Sat/Sun) and isoWeek. Bands: status in (approved, pending) intersecting the window, carrying the TRUE startDate/endDate plus startsBeforeWindow/endsAfterWindow, kind 'vacation', the frozen workingDays (never recounted), and the request id. Holidays: every Holiday dated inside the window whatever its country, each with appliesToAllInView computed against the rows THIS response carries; each member row carries the holidayIds that reached it, resolved server-side through resolveMemberHolidayCountry + isHolidayApplicableToMember, and countryCode = the RESOLVED country. Load the organization's countryCode once per request, not per member. The body carries no financial field and no MemberProfile field (TC-01-INT-01 asserts their absence over the whole body). meta = { scope, memberCount }. Register the controller and the service flat in app.module.ts beside HolidaysController/HolidaysService. T4 adds its own pair to the same two lists — take that edit here if you implement T3 first, and leave the file alone in T4.

concurrency.lock: none — the calendar writes nothing (State Machine invariant 1). It reads Membership, ProjectMember, VacationRequest, Holiday and Organization in one request with no transaction; every rule is evaluated on read, so a holiday deleted or a country set between two fetches simply shows in the next one (Edge cases 12, 13, 19).

tasks.title: GET and PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/settings/country — the organization's country
tasks.detail: A pair beside SigningSettingsController, at api/organizations/:orgId/settings/country, guarded by SessionGuard + OrgScopeGuard only. The capability check runs IN THE SERVICE, unlike its signing neighbour, because both halves answer 404 and CapabilityGuard answers 403: `view-holidays` for the GET (REQ-01-047) and `manage-holidays` for the PUT (REQ-01-035), each a bare NotFoundException, the HolidaysService.requireViewCapability / requireManageCapability shape. Both read and write Organization by session.organizationId, never the path id. GET returns { countryCode } — the stored value, null when nobody has stated one. PUT takes { countryCode } where null or '' clears it (REQ-01-034), validates with validateStatedCountryCode (T2, Validation Rule 9 - empty clears; anything else must be exactly two uppercase letters AND a code the assigned ISO 3166-1 list carries, so 'pl' and 'XX' are both refused), refuses a bad one with 422 { error: 'validation_error', fields: { countryCode: PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid } } (REQ-01-036), and returns the same body the GET does, carrying the value now stored. Register both in app.module.ts's controllers and providers (that file is T3's — make the edit in whichever task runs first). REPLAN, round 2 - an ABSENT countryCode key on this PUT clears the column, and that is a decision, not an accident of the validator: this route is a one-field settings resource whose GET and PUT carry the same representation, so a PUT with no country submits an empty country (REQ-01-034). The member write beside it is deliberately the other way round (T5), because its body carries three fields and a caller that ignores the new one must change nothing. Both rules are stated here so the difference reads as intended rather than as drift. AUTHORIZATION: both capability checks are handed the NORMALIZED role - can(normalizeRole(caller.role), 'view-holidays') and can(normalizeRole(caller.role), 'manage-holidays'). The database stores admin or member; the target set is admin | manager | user | viewer. 'admin' normalizes to admin and holds both; a stored 'member' normalizes to user, which holds neither, so it is answered 404 on both halves - the same answer a viewer gets, and the same answer the holiday list beside it already gives that row.

concurrency.lock: none, by REQ-01-033 — last-write-wins on one column with no read-modify-write, so there is nothing to lose. Other writers of this row: SigningSettingsService.update (a different column), and MembersService.remove (members.service.ts:160) and MembersService.updateDetail (members.service.ts:404), both of which hold `SELECT id FROM "Organization" ... FOR UPDATE` for their zero-admin count. A concurrent country write therefore WAITS on one of those transactions and then applies; it never reads the row first, so it cannot lose an update to them.

tasks.title: The member's country on the shipped detail read and write
tasks.detail: Two shipped routes gain one field each and change in no other way — same guards, same statuses, same messages for everything they already carry. READ (getDetail, members.service.ts:312): add countryCode to the MemberDetail interface and to the explicit projection at :352. It is the STORED value, null included, never the resolved one (REQ-01-045), and it is unconditional — the route is gated by no capability and the field is not conditional on one, so a user and a viewer receive it too. WRITE (updateDetail, members.service.ts:390): add countryCode to MemberDetailUpdateInput and write it inside the EXISTING transaction and the existing organization-row FOR UPDATE at :404, adding no lock of its own. Presence decides: touch the column only when the key is present in the body (`'countryCode' in body`, the idiom HolidaysService.parseInput uses at holidays.service.ts:316), so a caller that omits it changes nothing — Backward Compatibility 3. An explicit null or '' stores null (REQ-01-043). Validate with validateStatedCountryCode (T2, Validation Rule 9 - the uppercase shape AND membership of the assigned ISO list, so 'pl' and 'XX' are both refused) and refuse a bad value with 400 { errors: { countryCode: PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid } } (REQ-01-051) — 400, the status this route already refuses an invalid role and an invalid job title with, and the { errors } shape it already uses for jobTitle; NOT the 422 the organization write answers. The whole route stays behind its existing `can(caller.role, 'edit-detail')` check, so a caller without it still gets 403 MEMBER_MESSAGES.editForbidden and the new field buys no new refusal (REQ-01-044). REQ-01-048 needs NO CODE: restore (members.service.ts:273) and the invitation-acceptance restore (invitations.service.ts:529) both write only status/joinedAt/role/jobTitle and neither clears countryCode — keep it that way, and let TC-01-INT-28 be what proves it. Do not add the field to MembersService.list. AUTHORIZATION: this route's gate is shipped and unchanged - can(caller.role, 'edit-detail') at members.service.ts:415, which is handed the RAW stored value. Leave it that way: normalizing it here would change who may edit a member, which is no part of this spec. Both stored values reach the same decision under the target set - 'admin' is spelled identically in both enums and holds edit-detail, and a stored 'member' holds it under neither reading (can('member', ...) is false because CAPABILITY_MATRIX has no 'member' row, and normalizeRole('member') is user, which does not hold edit-detail either). The new field therefore buys no new refusal and no new grant (REQ-01-044).

concurrency.lock: the existing `SELECT id FROM "Organization" WHERE id = ... FOR UPDATE` at members.service.ts:404, inside updateDetail's own $transaction — countryCode is written by the same tx.membership.update as role and jobTitle and adds no lock. Other writers of a Membership row: MembersService.remove (status, under the same organization lock at :160), MembersService.restore (:273), InvitationsService.accept (:504 create, :529 same-organization restore), SignupService and TestMembersController. None of them touches countryCode, which is what REQ-01-048 requires.
reread: the target membership is loaded inside the transaction (members.service.ts:406) and the role/admin count re-read there

tasks.title: Every call site that resolves a member's country adopts the chain — and none keeps a phone-country read
tasks.detail: The four shipping sites in the contracts' call-site table, each of which reads `account.phoneCountryCode ?? null` today and must read the stated columns through resolveMemberHolidayCountry instead, loading Membership.countryCode and the organization's countryCode alongside. After this task no code path resolves a holiday country from Account.phoneCountryCode; the column stays on Account for the phone field that owns it. Delete HolidaysService.normalizeResolvedCountry (holidays.service.ts:381) rather than leaving a second normalizer behind, and update the doc comments at holidays.service.ts:77 and reports.ts:489 that name the old source. One implementation of the rule, or REQ-01-026 is true on one screen and false on the others.
allCallSites: apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.service.ts#listHolidays (the scope=mine branch, :98-107) — resolves the country behind the Time Tracking calendar's holiday markers and the vacation-request modal's holiday hint. After: the caller's Membership.countryCode, else the organization's, else null; a null caller still gets every global row, and only that.

apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts#loadCaller (:530-553) — sets Caller.countryCode, which is the country the Time Off 'my' report and the Amounts Owed 'my' roster read. After: the caller's membership country, else the organization's.

apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts#resolveSubjectMemberships (:1028-1048) — the member roster shared by Amounts Owed and Time & Activity, and the one that moves money: a country-scoped holiday adds a paid 'Holiday · {name}' row per member it applies to (buildHolidayRow, reports.ts:518). After: each membership's own country, else the organization's, else null — which pays LESS than today for a member whose only country was their phone's, and MORE for one who had none and is now covered by the organization's. Both directions are the deploy-day step the README's Blast Radius names; neither is a code decision to make here.

apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts#buildTimeOffResponse (:1875-1886) — the membership-country union behind the Time Off 'organization_wide' holiday group. After: each active membership resolved through the chain; the union of what they resolve to is what that group covers.

concurrency.lock: none — all four are reads. The chain is evaluated on read, which is why setting or clearing either country repairs every reader at once and nothing has to be backfilled (Edge cases 12 and 19).

tasks.title: The calendar screen and the navigation row
tasks.detail: A 'use client' page that fetches /api/organizations/{orgId}/time-off/calendar with credentials 'same-origin' — no server action, no API route. Gate: `if (!can(normalizeRole(session.role), 'view-time-off-calendar')) notFound()`, the notFound() pattern the documents pages use (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/documents/page.tsx:116) rather than the holidays page's redirect, because TC-01-E2E-06 asserts the app's not-found handling. Sidebar: a 'Calendar' row with testId nav-time-off-calendar, href /org/{orgId}/time-off/calendar, pushed into the existing timeOff array ABOVE the Holidays row (Sidebar.tsx:153), gated on hasCapability(role, 'ViewTimeOffCalendar') and omitted otherwise — never drawn-and-disabled. Structure, top to bottom, per the mock and contracts>Screens: PageHeader with the range navigation in its right slot (calendar-prev, calendar-today, calendar-next, calendar-range-label); ReportControls from @devscribed/ds in its scope + children shape, holding TWO ToggleButtons in their `options` form — the three calendar-scope-* segments and the three calendar-window-* segments. Draw no segmented control of your own: ToggleButton owns the track, the pill, --shadow-toggle-active, the roving tab stop and the per-segment data-testid. The teams and people pickers are MultiFilter from apps/web/src/reports/ReportFilters.tsx (a Select isMulti with closeMenuOnSelect false), rendered only for their own scope; calendar-teams-picker lists an 'Unassigned' entry ABOVE the projects whose value is the sentinel 'none', which ticks like a project and may be the only tick. Options come from the shipped GET .../projects and GET .../members. Legend, then the grid. Defaults: scope=all and the Month window over the caller's current month; the range is in-page state and is NOT put in the URL. Window and range arithmetic comes from T2's exported presets, driven by session.account.firstDayOfWeek — Week and 2 weeks step one preset length, Month steps a whole calendar month and always runs first-to-last day of it (REQ-01-049), and calendar-today returns to the window holding today. A band is ONE element spanning every day from its start to its end, weekends and holidays included (REQ-01-023), solid for approved and hatched with a dashed border for pending, carrying T2's accessible name; adjacent bands are separated by their own 3px side margins. A holiday with appliesToAllInView shades the whole column, draws calendar-day-holiday-{date} and NAMES the holiday in calendar-day-header-{date} (REQ-01-030); one without marks only calendar-cell-holiday-{membershipId}-{date} on the members it reached and names nothing in the header (REQ-01-031). Saturday and Sunday columns are shaded from days[].isWeekend (REQ-01-032). No rows -> calendar-empty-state replaces the grid and the filter bar stays (REQ-01-037); rows but no bands -> the full grid, no empty state (REQ-01-038). Any 422 -> calendar-error-banner above the grid carrying the message (the first value of the response's `fields`), with the last good grid left on screen underneath. Loading -> a skeleton in the grid area with the filter bar still interactive. DS GAPS: declare --surface-timeoff-band, --border-timeoff-band, --text-timeoff-band and --name-col: 264px ONCE, in a .time-off-calendar block in apps/web/app/globals.css that also carries what inline styles cannot express — position: sticky on the member column, the horizontal scroll container below --layout-breakpoint-desktop — and read every one of them through var(). No colour and no size on this screen is a literal except the two 3px values the DS gaps table records (the band's side margin and the pending hatch stripe), each carrying a @literal comment with the reason. The band's height is --space-10 and its corner --radius-s. Render exactly the data-testids the contracts table names and no others: the static gate blocks on any data-testid the diff adds that the spec bundle does not name. REPLAN, round 2 - two rules the first pass got wrong. (a) THE ANCHOR IS THE CALLER'S TODAY, NOT THE BROWSER'S. The initial anchor and the calendar-today control both come from todayInTimeZone(session.account.timezone) (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:639, exported from the package root and already used exactly this way at apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/NewRequestModal.tsx:133), whose fallback for a null, empty or unrecognized zone is UTC - REQ-01-018's own fallback, and the same field the server resolves range.today from. A browser-clock anchor puts the today marker in no column at all for a caller whose zone has crossed midnight and the browser's has not, and REQ-01-049 requires the Today control to land on the window HOLDING the caller's today. Nothing about today on this screen is computed from new Date(). (b) A FAILED READ IS NOT AN EMPTY ONE. A transport failure - fetch rejecting, or any response the endpoint's 422 body shape does not describe - draws calendar-error-banner carrying HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.toastServerError ('Something went wrong. Please try again.'), the message the Holidays page this same change edits already uses for a failed read (settings/holidays/page.tsx:179). It must NEVER carry TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.emptyStateBody: the contracts' Error Messages table gives that string no route and the UI Description assigns it to the Empty (no rows) state alone, so drawing it on a read that never happened reports a fact about data nobody fetched. Only a 422 carrying fields draws the endpoint's own message (the first value of fields); every other outcome draws the generic one, which also keeps a raw framework string such as "Internal server error" off the screen. The last good grid stays underneath in both cases.

tasks.title: The two country pickers, on the two screens that already ship
tasks.detail: Settings > Holidays: one Select labelled 'Organization country' ABOVE the existing country filter, testid org-country-select, hinted from TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.orgCountryHint, with an org-country-save button beside it. Its options are the same list the holiday form uses (HOLIDAY_COUNTRY_OPTIONS from ./country-options, whose first entry is the empty value that clears). Its value on first paint comes from GET .../settings/country, fetched alongside the holiday list the page already loads; saving PUTs the same path and toasts on success. Both admin and manager get the control (the page is already a 404 for a user and a viewer, so there is no read-only rendering to draw). Member detail > About: one Select labelled 'Country', testid member-country-select, in the block that already holds the role picker and the job title, whose FIRST option is labelled from TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.memberCountryDefaultOption and whose value is '' — which is what a stored null renders as and what stores null. It saves through the member update the screen already submits: add countryCode to the existing PUT body and to the `dirty` computation (MemberDetailScreen.tsx:164), or a country-only change leaves the shipped Save button disabled and the change unsaveable. One save, one toast, no second form and no second button. Draw the control only when detail.canEditJobTitle is true — the shipped flag that already means 'active target and the caller holds edit-detail' — so a caller without edit-detail opens the tab and simply does not get it, and nothing is drawn read-only. Add countryCode to the screen's MemberDetail interface and seed the control from the loaded detail. Keep everything else on both screens exactly as it is: no existing markup, control or testid is removed, renamed or moved. REPLAN, round 2 - THE OPTION LIST. Under the settled Validation Rule 9 a country is refused unless the assigned ISO list carries it, and HOLIDAY_COUNTRY_OPTIONS is built from COUNTRY_OPTIONS (apps/web/src/account-data.ts:58), which is libphonenumber's getCountries() and offers AC, TA and XK - three codes validateCountryCode refuses. Both country pickers, org-country-select and member-country-select, therefore list only options their own save accepts: filter HOLIDAY_COUNTRY_OPTIONS through the assigned-list test where those two Selects build their options, keeping the labels and the ordering they already have and adding no second country list. The holiday list's country FILTER (holidays-country-filter) and the holiday form's own country picker are NOT filtered: a Holiday row may carry any two uppercase letters, and a filter that cannot name a row that exists is a worse control than one offering a rare country.

concurrency.lock: none — the writes are T4's and T5's

tasks.title: The cases — unit, integration, E2E, and the three helpers the Verification Plan says this spec owes
tasks.detail: Every case in 01-vacation-calendar.cases.md, at the level it names, referencing its TC id in the test name. UNIT (packages/validation): TC-01-UNIT-01 on resolveMemberHolidayCountry with all ten pairs — the last two, (null,'xx') and ('XX','YY'), are the branch that matters: with nothing usable left the chain returns null rather than the raw unusable string. TC-01-UNIT-02 on the range validator and the three presets from both firstDayOfWeek values. TC-01-UNIT-03 on isHolidayApplicableToMember (three of its six probes already exist in reports.test.ts:325-338 — add the case as its own, including the lowercase-'pl' member). TC-01-UNIT-04 on both capability unions under 'member', 'user' and 'viewer', ending with the unnormalized can('member', ...) probe that must be false. INTEGRATION: one new file apps/api/test/time-off-calendar.spec.ts carrying all 29 cases including TC-01-INT-29, which calls GET /holidays?scope=mine and is the proof that the calendar's resolution answers on the screen beside it. Build state with prisma directly, the way apps/api/test/holidays.spec.ts does (createMember at :57 already takes phoneCountryCode and timezone — TC-01-INT-12 and TC-01-INT-29 need a phone country seeded precisely to prove it now reaches nothing, and TC-01-INT-19 needs Account.timezone set to Pacific/Kiritimati, Pacific/Niue and null). TC-01-INT-19 computes each zone's date for the run's own instant and writes no literal date. TC-01-INT-01 asserts over the WHOLE body that no financial field and no MemberProfile field appears. TC-01-INT-27: assert countryCode is present and equal for the user and the viewer alongside the target-derived fields — do not deep-equal the two bodies, because the shipped projection carries callerRole, canEditRole and availableRoles, which are properties of the caller. E2E: one new file e2e/tests/time-off-calendar.spec.ts with the eight cases, plus THREE helpers this spec owes to e2e/tests/helpers.ts — promote createHolidayViaApi out of e2e/tests/reports-time-off.spec.ts:38 (leave that suite importing the shared one), and add setMemberCountryViaApi and setOrganizationCountryViaApi. Every fixture that creates more than one member must `login(request, adminEmail)` before each inviteAndAcceptViaApi: accepting an invitation switches the cookie jar to the new member, and the second invitation is otherwise 403. Invite with the four-role enum ('user', 'viewer'); 'member' is refused with 400. The cases name literal September 2026 dates: reach that month from the screen's default (the caller's current month) by stepping calendar-prev/calendar-next a computed number of times — zero while the run's date is in that month — rather than assuming the default lands there. REPLAN, round 2 - the two cases the settled rule rewrote, and one assertion that pins the old message. TC-01-INT-21 submits POL, then 1, then pl, then XX, then PL, and reads the country back after the XX attempt: 422 PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid for the first four, the read-back still answering the value stored before XX, then 200 for PL stored as PL. TC-01-INT-25 ends with pl AND XX on the member write, both refused with 400 PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid and the stored country left null - XX is the one that matters, because its shape is right and storing it would leave a country every read discards. Any assertion naming HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.countryCodeInvalid for these two ROUTES is now wrong: apps/api/test/time-off-calendar.spec.ts:1131 pins that text today and must pin 'Enter a valid country' instead. HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.countryCodeInvalid stays asserted where a holiday ROW's own country is written (apps/api/test/holidays.spec.ts:607), which this spec does not touch - keep that assertion exactly as it is, because it is what catches one validator being swapped for the other.

tasks.title: The four shipped suites whose fixture is the source this spec drops
tasks.detail: Four shipped cases seed a member's country as Account.phoneCountryCode and assert the national holiday that follows from it. REQ-01-026 drops that source, so each fails until its FIXTURE moves to the stated column — the assertions do not change and none may be removed. (1) apps/api/test/holidays.spec.ts, TC-03-INT-14, the case at :381 with its fixture at :402 — 'by@acme.com' is created with phoneCountryCode 'BY' and expects Labour Day + Victory Day from scope=mine; set Membership.countryCode = 'BY' on that member instead (the createMember helper at :57 can take a membership country beside the account one) and leave the phone value in place where the case has one, so the case now also witnesses that the phone reaches nothing. (2) apps/api/test/reports-amounts-owed.spec.ts, its TC-01-INT-12 at :573 and TC-01-INT-13 at :607 — the BY member and the US member get their countries stated on the membership. (3) apps/api/test/reports-time-off.spec.ts, the 'viewer calling /my returns only holidays for their country' case at :404 — same move for the BY viewer. (4) e2e/tests/holidays.spec.ts, TC-03-E2E-04 at :296 — it calls setOwnCountryViaApi(request, 'BY') at :309 and then asserts the weekly calendar's marker; state the country on the membership through T9's setMemberCountryViaApi instead (an admin call, so log the admin back in first) and keep setOwnCountryViaApi only if some other case still needs a phone number. Do not touch any other assertion in these files, and add no new case here — the new rule's own cases are T9's. REPLAN, round 2 - THE FIXTURES MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL. In all three API suites, a fixture that states a membership country must not carry the SAME country on Account.phoneCountryCode: drop the phone value, or give it a different country. A fixture seeding both to one country cannot fail if the code regressed to reading the phone, which is the only rule these four suites are being edited for. Where a case keeps a phone country on purpose (holidays.spec.ts TC-03-INT-14, reports-amounts-owed.spec.ts, reports-time-off.spec.ts), it must be a DIFFERENT country from the stated one, so the assertion witnesses that the phone reaches nothing rather than merely agreeing with it.

risks.risk: The country change is silent where it is loudest: Amounts Owed pays a holiday row per member a country-scoped holiday applies to, and after this ships every member whose only country was their phone's resolves to null and stops receiving those rows until somebody states a country.
risks.mitigation: Nothing is stored wrong — the chain is evaluated on read, so stating the organization country repairs every such member at once. T6 changes only the source; the deploy-day step is the README's, not the code's. T10 keeps the shipped suites asserting the same outcomes through the new source, which is what would otherwise hide the change behind four red tests.

risks.risk: Four shipped test files are edited by a run that owns none of them, which reads like a suite being bent to fit.
risks.mitigation: T10 is a task of its own, naming each file, each case and each line, and changes fixtures only — no assertion is removed or weakened, which the static gate also counts.

risks.risk: The E2E cases name literal September 2026 dates while the suite runs on whatever day it runs.
risks.mitigation: Reach the month by stepping calendar-prev/calendar-next a number computed from the run's own date rather than assuming the default window lands there; that is zero clicks today and correct in any month.

risks.risk: Three country rules now sit side by side and reaching for the wrong one is silent. The two STATED columns are written under Validation Rule 9 (uppercase shape AND the assigned list; 'pl' and 'XX' both refused; PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid). A HOLIDAY row's country keeps validateHolidayCountryCode (any two uppercase letters; HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.countryCodeInvalid). The READ is the forgiving one (resolveMemberHolidayCountry upcases and tests the assigned list). The asymmetry is the document's own decision: a stored code the read discards removes holiday pay in silence, while a holiday labelled with an unassigned country simply reaches nobody.
risks.mitigation: T2 exports rule 9 once and both writes call it; holidays.service.ts:322 and HolidayModal.tsx:222 are left alone. TC-01-INT-21 and TC-01-INT-25 pin the write side including 'XX'; TC-01-UNIT-01 pins the read side ('pl' -> PL, 'XX' -> skipped); apps/api/test/holidays.spec.ts:607 still pins the holiday row's own message, which is what catches one validator being swapped for the other.

risks.risk: The member country rides a Save button the shipped screen disables when nothing looks dirty, so a country-only change could be unsaveable.
risks.mitigation: T8 adds countryCode to the dirty computation at MemberDetailScreen.tsx:164. The button stays a genuine in-flight/no-op guard and is never disabled for validation.

risks.risk: The teams picker's options come from GET .../projects, which returns only their own assigned active projects to a user while the endpoint itself scopes rows by the named projects for any caller who holds the capability.
risks.mitigation: The spec does not say what the picker lists, and this is the shipped list every other screen uses; the endpoint's own rule (REQ-01-006) is unaffected. Recorded so a reviewer sees it as the existing behaviour rather than a new decision.

risks.risk: The country picker the two screens reuse is built from libphonenumber's country list and offers AC, TA and XK, which the settled write rule refuses - a control offering a value its own save cannot store.
risks.mitigation: T8 filters both country Selects through the assigned-list test and leaves the holiday form's picker and the holiday list's country filter as they are.

risks.risk: The screen's anchor and the server's range.today are two computations of one value, and nothing in the payload forces them to agree.
risks.mitigation: T7 makes both read Account.timezone: the server through its own resolver, the screen through todayInTimeZone(session.account.timezone), which is the same field with the same UTC fallback. The marker is drawn by comparing a day against the server's range.today, so the screen never decides which day is today - only which window to open on.
